evidence: Cic. Inv. 1.42: ēventus est alicujus exitus negōtiī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: How a thing turns out, well or badly. Latin often says the result with a clause instead: ex quō fit ut, ita fit ut, with the result that; quid ēvēnerit, what came of it.

evidence: Caes. BC 3.22: celerem et facilem exitum habuērunt (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Tusc. 4.19: ex quō fit ut pudōrem rubor, terrōrem pallor et tremor cōnsequātur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The result is the subject, the cause the object: blushing “follows” shame.

evidence: Cic. Sen. 72: ex quō fit, ut animōsior etiam senectūs sit quam adulēscentia
Cic. Off. 1.101: ita fit, ut ratiō praesit

phrases.english: the result showed that fortune favours the brave

phrases.latin: ex quō fit, ut animōsior etiam senectūs sit quam adulēscentia et fortior
phrases.english: and the result is that old age is bolder and braver even than youth
the result is the teacher of fools

sources: Lewis & Short: eventus · Lewis & Short: exitus · Lewis & Short: consequor
